sb_something_below.description:
You! Yes, you. I'm only up at the Waystation for rope, so let's be quick.

Fizzwick Boltcog. I found the Sinkhole Crater last spring and I have been digging in it since, which my former partner describes as an obsession and I describe as a schedule.

I found a stair at the bottom. A STAIR. Cut, dressed, going down.

I found a great deal of glittering rock, which I will not be discussing.

And three days ago I found what I have written up in my own notes as 'a series of unfortunate bites'.

Sinkhole burrowers. They came up through the floor of my own dig, which is the one direction I had not budgeted for.

They are still coming.

Little brown things, lots of legs, extremely rude.

Thin them and I'll get back to work.

And no, you can't see what I've found. Nothing personal. You just can't.
sb_something_below.accept_text: Out at my dig in the Sinkhole Crater, south-east of the Waystation. They come up through the floor.

sb_amber_for_the_taking.description:
Now the part of this dig that pays for the rest of the dig.

The hive builds in amber.

And amber - I'll keep this brief, I'm told I don't - is worth more by the ounce than every single thing I have pulled out of that crater to date, combined, including the stair, which cannot be sold.

The weavers spin it. The spitters spit it. The best shards sit in the gland before either happens, which is why you want them off the creature and not off a wall.

I'd go myself. I have gone myself. That's how I know about the gland and it is also how I know about the spitters.

Don't drop them.

A shard that's cracked isn't worth a tenth, and they crack on gravel, and that entire crater is gravel.

I have thought about that problem for a month and the solution is apparently 'be careful'.
sb_amber_for_the_taking.accept_text: Off the hive weavers and resin spitters in the rings of the Broodspiral, under the Sinkhole Crater south-east of the Waystation.

sb_windspire_harpies.description:
Alamir. I've come in off the Hoodoo Spires to restock arrows, and I'm going straight back out.

The spires in the north-east are full of wind and voices, and I've stopped being able to tell you which is which.

Harpies nest in the hollows up there. They shriek down at anything that passes underneath, and it is not a warning and it is not territorial - I've watched them do it to an empty road.

I've hunted them a season.

My arrows are running low. My patience went some while before that, and I'd rather be honest about the order.

Feathers, claws, and a great deal of noise, out of the hollows on the east side.

And don't stand under the spires.

They drop things. Not on purpose, I don't think. It doesn't improve the outcome.

sb_hyenas_in_the_bones.turn_in_text:
Mmm. You know what I'll hear out there tomorrow? Nothing.

You'd be surprised how good that sounds after a season of it.

sb_the_matriarchs_last_walk.turn_in_text:
It's done, then.

Quietly, I hope.

Take this. And say a word for her on the road, if you've got one in you.

sb_thrumbone.turn_in_text:
They tell me the ground out there's gone quiet. First time in years.

I... thank you.

Take these. They belong to the plain now, and so do you, whether or not that's what you wanted.

sb_eyes_on_the_gate.description:
Zhuul. I came down to the Waystation for a hot meal and a dry night, and I'm back up to the Keep at dawn.

I've been lying in the grass east of Bael'dun Keep for two months with a spyglass and a bad attitude, and I'd like it noted that one of those is professional.

The dwarves have turned Bael'dun into a proper fortress. Riflemen up on the walls, patrols working the yard on a rotation I could set a clock by.

That's not a mining camp protecting itself. That's a garrison.

I need the gate scouted and the riflemen thinned before one of them spots me, which is a matter of time rather than luck at this point.

Walk up to the gate. Look. Come back.

If a rifleman objects, shoot him first.

I'd go myself. I'd leave a trail through that grass you could follow from the wall.

Trolls are tall, mon. It's the one part of the job I can't train out.
sb_eyes_on_the_gate.accept_text: Bael'dun Keep, north-west of the Waystation. The gate you want is on its east side. Walk up, look, come back.

sb_cut_the_fuse.accept_text: North-west of the Waystation, along the charge-line that runs up to the Keep's east gate. The experts wear red hats. Take the charges off them.

sb_ironvein.accept_text: Bael'dun Keep, north-west of the Waystation. He walks the east wall among his sergeants. Listen for the hammer.

nb_rig_crews.description:
Nix. Sludge inspector, which is a title I made up, for a job nobody's hiring.

I worked for the Venture Company. Years. Good years, honestly - I'm not going to pretend I was miserable, because the lie would show.

Then I found out what they were doing down in the fen.

Now I sit in a rusted shack out by the fen and count crews, and come in to Far Watch to report it, which is a career trajectory I'd advise against.

They're drilling day and night. The ground is bleeding black and it's reaching the water, and I've been watching the edge of the stain move for eleven months.

I want the crews gone.

And - this is the part I need you to hear properly - preferably without anyone I like standing in the way.

I know most of them. I trained some of them. I'm asking anyway, which is the whole of what I've got to give this fen.

The drillers are the loud ones. Stop the noise and the guards come out, and the guards are quieter and nastier.
nb_rig_crews.accept_text: At the rig in the Sludge Fen, north of Far Watch. The drillers are the loud ones.

nb_heart_of_the_vein.description:
Now something I can only get from inside, and it's the thing I actually came out to the Lode for.

The elementals in that mine are made of the same rock as the walls. Same stone, same seams - and the walls are laced with crystal all the way through.

So they carry the vein in them. Break one open and you're holding a core sample that nobody had to cut.

If I can read those, I can tell you how much the Company has already taken out of my claim. Not estimate. Tell you, to within a season.

That's a number I can put in front of somebody in Orgrimmar who outranks a clipboard.

Break them open. You'll find a glowing core in each one.

Bring me a handful - a single core is a spot, a row of them is a vein, and I need the vein.
nb_heart_of_the_vein.accept_text: Off the rock elementals in the galleries of the Boulder Lode Mine, north of Far Watch.

nb_hounds_of_the_oasis.description:
Mahri. I run the scouts out of Far Watch, and most of them are watching the Stagnant Oasis right now.

The Stagnant Oasis hasn't been fit to drink from in years. Everyone knows that. It still draws every wanderer on the plains, because people will walk toward water they've been told is bad on the grounds that somebody must have been exaggerating.

Lately it draws something else.

Dervish hounds. Lean, mange-ridden things the Kolkar dervishes breed and set loose out here - not to guard anything. To be loose.

They circle first and bite after, and the circling is the part that gets people, because it goes on long enough that you start thinking about something else.

Keep your back to something solid. A cliff, a tent, anything.

I want them gone before they work out what a campfire is for.

nb_pickets_past_the_wall.description:
Captain Korvash. I've come down off the Rampart for an hour, and I'll be back up on it by dark.

The Rampart is the Horde's wall against the Kaldorei, and I'll tell you the thing nobody puts in a dispatch: it's a wall with a very thin side.

That strip just north of the gate is the thin side.

Sentinel pickets hold it. Archers cover them from the cliffs. And between them they shoot anything that comes within a hundred paces of our own gate, which means we are not holding a wall, we are living behind one.

I've been polite about this for two seasons. I've sent letters.

I'm done being polite.

Clear the strip.

The pickets hold the line and the archers cover them, so take the archers first if you can manage it.

Don't be proud about the order. Proud is how the last two went.

nb_signal_horns.description:
Every sentinel picket out there carries a signal horn.

One blast and the whole forest answers. Not a patrol - the forest. I've heard it once, from the Rampart gate, and I've organised two seasons of orders around never hearing it again.

I want them off the field before the Kaldorei work out how thin this Rampart actually is.

Because that's the real position, and I'd rather you knew it going out. We're not holding them back. We're holding a line they have not yet decided to test properly, and a horn is how the deciding would start.

Cut them off the belts. Quick, before they get them up.

Bring them to me. I want to see them in a pile - and I want to count them, because the count is the only measure I've got of how much time we just bought.

nb_warden_ilthae.description:
Their commander at the Rampart is Warden Ilthae.

Old. Steady. Silver-haired, and she has not lost a skirmish in twenty years, which I know because I've been on the wrong end of four of them and I keep a record.

I respect her. I'd like that said once, plainly, and then I'd like it not to come up again.

She does not waste her people. Every time I have pushed at that strip she has given me exactly enough ground to make the push expensive and not one step more, and she has never once chased me when chasing would have cost her.

That is a better officer than I am. I've thought about it enough.

I'd still like her dead, because she is the thing standing between the Horde and this road, and respect was never the same as agreement.

She's got a glaive, a bad temper and no fear at all.

Don't fight her in the open. Don't fight her at all, if you can avoid it.

But you can't.

nb_slugs_in_the_reeds.description:
Dugmok. Warden of the fens, which used to be the quietest posting in the Barrens and no longer is.

The Slug Fens were only ever slow, wet and quiet. That's the whole of what those fens were. You could walk the causeway with your eyes shut and the worst thing that happened was your boots.

Then the slugs got big.

I don't know why. Nobody does, and I've asked three shaman and a goblin, and the goblin wanted paying.

Pale, fat, and bigger than a dog now, and they're creeping across the causeway at night.

My wardens keep that causeway open. That's the job and it's the only job.

Because nobody wants to be the one who explains why a caravan went in and the cargo came out as soup.

Cut them back off it. If they wriggle, hit harder.

nb_venom_glands.description:
Now a thing I want and will not fetch myself, and I'd rather say that plainly than dress it up as delegation.

The fen slugs carry a venom gland in the back. Green sac, about the size of a fist on the big ones.

Cured right, it makes a first-rate poison. I know how. My mother knew how and her hands were steadier than mine have been for about four years.

So: cut them out whole.

Whole, hear me. Don't pop them.

If one goes while you're carrying it we'll be burying a tauren, and the ceremony is long and I'd be at it instead of here.

The next caravan through that causeway is going to want every advantage it can carry.
nb_venom_glands.accept_text: Off the fen slugs along the causeway through the Slug Fens, south of Mor'shan. Cut them out whole.

cb_strays_on_the_plain.description:
Magra Dustwalker. I've brought the herd in to Grol'dom Farm for a few nights, because the plain's not safe for them.

I've run kodo north of the Crossroads for twenty years.

It has never been this bad, and I've said that out loud exactly twice, both times this season.

The hyenas have learned something. That's the part that frightens me, not the teeth.

They've worked out that a calf separated from the herd is a calf that does not come home - and so they don't attack. They shadow us. At a distance, all day, patient as a debt collector, and they take whatever lags.

Nothing taught them that. They arrived at it.

They're out on the plain. Brown-grey, spotted, grinning.

They will not run from you. They've never once had a reason to.

cb_dreadmist_approach.description:
Scout Zarla. I've come in to Grol'dom to sleep under a roof for once, so I'll be quick.

Dreadmist Peak is the grey massif in the north-west corner of the plain, and the cultists inside it have been very quiet lately.

I want to be clear that quiet is the problem.

I've watched that approach for a week. When they're raiding, there's traffic - runners out, carts in, a certain amount of shouting about rope. I know what a busy cult looks like.

There's been almost nothing for six days, and the few that do come out are walking in step.

A cult that's stopped doing things has finished preparing to do one thing.

Follow the road past the third baobab, up to where the cliffs close in. Their banners hang at the canyon mouth.

Look. Don't linger.

And don't touch the banners. I'll explain why when you're back, if I turn out to be right.

cb_voidcaller_veshra.turn_in_text:
The ritual faltered. My people on the ridge felt it.

Something snapped, and the whole canyon went quiet in a way it hasn't been all week.

Take this. Well earned.
cb_voidcaller_veshra.accept_text: At the ritual circle in the canyon mouth of Dreadmist Peak, north of Grol'dom. Cultists first.

cb_imps_in_the_brush.accept_text: Off the imps in the brush below Dreadmist Peak, north of Grol'dom. Wear gloves.

cb_old_sunhide.accept_text: On the plain toward the Sentinel Rocks, north-east of the farm. Thin his herd first.
cb_old_sunhide.description:
Every herder's story has a villain in it. I'd like to be honest with you about mine before you go.

Old Sunhide is a bull giraffe the height of a watchtower, with a hide exactly the colour of the dry grass he stands in.

He doesn't hunt. He's never killed anything in his life and he wouldn't know how.

He wanders. And wherever he wanders, calves end up flat, because a thing that size does not look down and a calf does not look up.

So I don't hold it against him. Not exactly. He hasn't done anything a giraffe shouldn't do.

I'm just tired of burying calves, and I've reached the age where tired is enough of a reason.

He walks the plain out toward the Sentinel Rocks. You'll see him a long way off - and you'll want to, because nothing that size should be able to come up on you quietly, and he can.

Thin his herd first, to take the cover away. Then him.

cb_sentinel_stingers.description:
The Sentinel Rocks - the sandstone teeth north-east of the farm.

Best shelter on these plains. The only shade a herd can lie down in between here and the hills, and every herder I've ever known has used it.

No kodo has slept there in three weeks.

Redstone scorpids have taken the crevices. That alone I could work around - you move the herd, you lose a season, you don't lose animals.

But something bigger has taken the scorpids.

I've been up close enough to see how they're behaving and they're not holding that ground for themselves. There's a brood-queen in those rocks and they're hers.

Red-brown, the size of a dog, tail like a sickle.

And the big mother, if she shows her face.

She will. They always do, once you've made a mess of the nursery.
cb_sentinel_stingers.accept_text:
The Sentinel Rocks, north-east of Grol'dom Farm. In the crevices.

Their matriarch is the big one in the deepest crevice. The herd will not come back while she is there.

nb_claim_jumpers.accept_text: The lower galleries of the Boulder Lode Mine, north of Far Watch.

nb_curved_blades.accept_text: Off the Kolkar dervishes at the Stagnant Oasis, south-west of Far Watch. Don't clean them.

nb_engineer_whirleygig.accept_text: The back of the rig's workshop in the Sludge Fen, north of Far Watch. Guards first, then him.

nb_foreman_grills.accept_text: The crystal chamber at the top of the Boulder Lode Mine, north of Far Watch. Overseers hold the way up.

nb_old_mire_maw.accept_text: The deep pools at the end of the causeway through the Slug Fens, south of Mor'shan.

nb_peat_hearts.accept_text: The deep Slug Fens, south of Mor'shan, off the causeway at night. Hit the middle.

nb_pressure_gauges.accept_text: Off the pumpjack guards at the rig in the Sludge Fen, north of Far Watch. They keep them on a belt chain.

nb_prospector_delvik.accept_text: A side adit off the middle gallery of the Boulder Lode Mine, behind the rubble. The mine's north of Far Watch.

nb_sludge_samples.accept_text: Off the sludge elementals where the oil's pooled in the Sludge Fen, north of Far Watch. Take it from the middle.

nb_sprites_in_the_seams.accept_text: In the crystal seams of the Boulder Lode Mine, north of Far Watch. Hit them while they pause to sparkle.

nb_stormcallers.accept_text: The far side of the Stagnant Oasis, south-west of Far Watch. Break the dervish ring, then the casters.

nb_supervisor_lugwizzle.accept_text:
The pumphouse at the rig in the Sludge Fen, north of Far Watch. He's usually inside, shouting.

His oil drillers will be in there with him.

nb_verog_the_dervish.accept_text: At the heart of the Stagnant Oasis, south-west of Far Watch. Clear the dervishes round him first.

sb_down_the_stair.accept_text: The stair at the edge of the Sinkhole Crater, south-east of the Waystation. Keep to the right-hand wall.

sb_giants_knucklebones.accept_text: Off the bone-dust wraiths among the ribs on the Field of Giants, south of the Waystation.

sb_mastiffs_at_the_gate.accept_text: Outside the walls of Bael'dun Keep, north-west of the Waystation. The mastiffs and the sergeants walking them.

sb_screen_the_queen.accept_text: The Larval Screen in the Broodspiral, the last ring before the Hollow. The crater's south-east of the Waystation.

sb_the_tenders.accept_text: The brood chamber past the outer ring of the Broodspiral, south-east of the Waystation. Stay out of the green.

sb_tunnel_guards.accept_text: Below the burrowers in the Sinkhole Crater, south-east of the Waystation, holding the way to the stair.

sb_vexa.accept_text: The nest at the centre of the Sinkhole Crater, south-east of the Waystation, below the guards.

sb_voices_in_the_spires.accept_text: Off the harpy windcallers in the Hoodoo Spires, north-east of the Waystation. The dust devils follow the singing.

sb_the_raptor_cull.description:
East of the Waystation, south of the spires, is the Raptor Grounds. A long valley between two ridges, and the Sunscale nest the whole length of it.

I'm a hunter. So I'll tell you what this is before I ask, because I've had people take it the wrong way and go in there like it was a war.

It's a cull.

The grounds are overfull this season. Too many stalkers on the ridges, too many lashtails down in the valley, and nowhere near enough prey to carry them through to spring.

Left alone they'll eat the valley hollow and then starve in it, and the grounds don't come back from that inside a generation.

So: stalkers on the ridges, lashtails in the valley.

And leave the eggs.

I mean that as an instruction and not a kindness. I won't have it said I broke the balance - I'm correcting one.
sb_the_raptor_cull.accept_text: The Raptor Grounds, east of the Waystation. Leave the eggs.
